ONE TRANSACTION HISTORY
Policy changes/Premium adjustments/Carrier reporting

FIT BORDEON INTO YOUR OPERATIONS

Start with your workflow.
Make the handovers clear.

Begin with one book, binder or placement workflow. Agree where the data comes from, what Bordeon maintains and what your carrier or finance team receives.

01 / YOUR EXISTING INFORMATION

Bring a representative example.

Walk through an anonymised Excel file or system export with us: policy references, agreed premium, commission and carrier shares. Together we identify the source of each field.

02 / ONE CONNECTED RECORD

Record the change once.

Enter an agreed endorsement and premium adjustment against the policy. Bordeon retains the previous version and calculates commission, net premium and carrier allocation from the recorded amounts and shares.

03 / TRACEABLE OUTPUT

Reuse the transactions in the report.

Generate a CSV bordereau from unreported transactions. Keep the saved report and its carrier obligations linked to the policy history, without rebuilding the same calculations in separate files.

How do our existing files and systems fit?

We agree the source of record, field mapping, transfer method and responsibilities before implementation. The interactive demo uses manual entry of accepted business and agreed adjustments. Any file ingestion, integration or carrier-specific output is explicitly scoped and confirmed for your setup.

Which work does Bordeon take out of the process?

Once the transaction is recorded, commission and carrier shares flow into the report and its obligations. Earlier policy versions and report snapshots stay available, so your team can trace an amount without reconstructing it from separate versions of a spreadsheet.

WHEN A CHANGE ARRIVES AFTER REPORTING

The report is sent.
Then the policy changes.

An endorsement arrives after the first bordereau has been shared. Keep that report intact, record the agreed adjustment and show exactly what belongs in the next report.

A FAMILIAR OPERATIONS QUESTION

“What changed since
the last report?”

The original €120,000 premium has already been reported. An endorsement adds €10,000. Bordeon keeps the first report at €102,000 net and links the new €8,500 net adjustment to the next report, with €5,100 and €3,400 allocated to the two carriers.

INSURANCE EXPERIENCE & REGULATORY CONTEXT

The detail matters.
We know the responsibility.

Our experience comes from working on the carrier side and with the underlying insurance information. It shapes how we approach policy records, premium movements and reporting handovers.

TRANSACTION TRACEABILITY

Keep the supporting record.

Follow an amount back to its policy version, premium transaction and report snapshot. Retain the history your team needs when a carrier asks what changed.

CARRIER REPORTING

Work from the requirements.

Define the required fields, reporting periods, carrier formats and review responsibilities for the agreed workflow. The setup starts with the information counterparties actually need.

DATA & OPERATIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Make the responsibilities explicit.

Before implementation, review data handling, access, retention, hosting and operational resilience requirements with your team. Document the controls and responsibilities required for your setup.

Regulatory requirements in context

Requirements depend on the business, jurisdiction and delegated authority arrangements. For Lloyd’s delegated authority business, reporting standards cover risk, premium and claims information, with additional requirements depending on the circumstances. We agree the policy and premium reporting scope relevant to your operation.

Data protection and ICT risk requirements, including GDPR and DORA where applicable, form part of the implementation discussion. We assess the applicable requirements, supporting evidence and responsibilities for your specific arrangement, and agree the controls needed before implementation.
